In its FY2025 10-K risk factors, Johnson & Johnson says the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) has changed Medicare Part D benefit design. It says the IRA has subjected certain of its products to government-established pricing beginning in 2026, and that more products may be subject in the future. J&J also warns of penalty exposure tied to pending litigation, and says Part D changes could hurt U.S. Innovative Medicine sales.
